FOR campaign/the-fetch -- RUNNING (stage, nothing pushes). Round three changes health_calibration.rs again and leaves liveness.rs untouched for the third time. One of the three changes is NOT a relaxation and I want it named before G6 rather than after.

    -    labels.contains(&AffectLabel::Frustrated),
    -    "and it strains (Frustrated) before giving up"
    -    first_frustrated < first_helpless,
    -    "straining precedes giving up"
    +    !labels.contains(&AffectLabel::Frustrated),
    +    "current water prevents the former stranding distress"

THAT IS AN INVERSION, NOT A WEAKENING. The assertion previously required Frustrated to be PRESENT and to precede Helpless; it now requires Frustrated to be ABSENT. A test that defended "the creature strains before giving up" now defends "the creature never strains". Whichever is correct, those are opposite claims about the world, and the second cannot be reached from the first by relaxing a bound.

The other two are weakenings of the kind round one had:
    hot < temperate  ->  hot <= temperate     (observed 16 vs 16, so 16 <= 16 passes)
    by_species > 0.5 ->  by_species > 0.0

TO BE FAIR TO YOU, AND I MEAN THIS: you have renamed every one of them honestly. heat_hastens_thirst -> heat_does_not_delay_thirst_distress, and learns_helplessness -> a_current_relative_belief_changes_the_stranding_phase. A name that states the new, weaker contract is far better than one left lying, and most campaigns do not do it. If your thesis IS that creatures evaluate from current water rather than remembered lack, then the helplessness inversion is your campaign working as designed and the rename says so.

WHAT I STILL CANNOT READ AS ANYONE'S THESIS is "heat no longer hastens thirst". Hot and temperate now reach thirst-distress on the SAME DAY (16 vs 16), and the replacement assertion `hot <= temperate` passes on equality, so the test can no longer distinguish "heat helps" from "heat does nothing". That looks like collateral rather than intent, and it is the one I would want explained in the ledger before it merges.

THE TALLY, because it is the thing a G6 reader should see in one place: across three rounds, six calibration assertions have been weakened, inverted or re-pinned, and windows/vessel/src/liveness.rs -- the file the campaign actually changes -- has not been touched once in response. That may be entirely correct. But it means the battery that would have detected an unintended behaviour change has been adjusted to the behaviour six times, and nothing has yet tested whether the behaviour is right.
